chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him, 'Does the woman lead the women in prayer?' He said, 'No, except for the deceased woman, if there is no one more entitled than her to lead her. She stands in the middle of them in the row with them, and she says Takbir and they say Takbir.'
ai.seo_question: Where does a woman stand when leading other women in funeral prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the specific protocol for female leadership in funeral prayers, restricting the role to cases where no closer male relative is available. It highlights the distinct spatial arrangement where the woman leads from the center of the row, emphasizing equality in ritual participation while maintaining structural distinctions from male-led prayers.
